newsitem.title: CHINA: China says most banks separated from trust firms.
newsitem.headline: China says most banks separated from trust firms.

text.p: Most of 186 trust and investment firms affiliated with China's four largest state banks are now managed separately from the banks under a policy to keep the two sectors apart, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
Xinhua said the total value of trust firm assets removed from the four big commercial banks was about 100 billion yuan ($12 billion).

As of November last year, some 46 trust and investment firms had been sold or had their operations split from the Industrial and Commercial Bank while 36 had been removed from the Agricultural Bank, Xinhua said quoting the central bank.
The Bank of China had withdrawn its control of 33 companies while the China Construction Bank had separated from another 33, the news agency said.
It added that 33 more trust firms had been approved for transfer from the four big banks.
Asset evaluations were still being carried out to transfer the remaining trust companies, Xinhua said. It did not specify what would happen to the remaining five firms.
Banks were barred from conducting trust and investment business under the Commercial Bank law which was passed by parliament in 1995, Xinhua said.
China has moved to separate banks from investment and trust companies in a bid to keep commercial banks from dealing in the country's stock markets. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
